claim: AWS Control Tower has overall concurrency limitations: in general, one operation at a time is permitted, with two exceptions (optional control operations and Account Factory account operations).
question: How many AWS Control Tower operations can run at the same time in general?

values.display: one operation at a time is permitted

qualifiers.condition: except optional control operations and Account Factory account operations

evidence.quote: In general, one operation at a time is permitted. Two exceptions to this limitation are allowed:

claim: Optional controls can be activated and deactivated concurrently, through an asynchronous process; up to 100 control-related operations can be in progress at a time in total, whether called from the console or from an API.
question: How many AWS Control Tower control operations can be in progress at the same time?

qualifiers.scope: per landing zone, console and API combined

evidence.quote: Up to one hundred (100) control-related operations at a time can be in progress, in total, no matter if they are called from the console or from an API.

note: d072. History 2024-05-20: increase of the concurrent control operations quota to 100 (old value not stated).

claim: Account Factory can provision, update and enroll accounts concurrently, with up to 5 account-related operations in progress at once; unmanaging accounts must be done one account at a time.
question: How many accounts can AWS Control Tower Account Factory provision, update or enroll at the same time?

qualifiers.condition: Account Factory; unmanaging is one account at a time

evidence.quote: Accounts can be provisioned, updated, and enrolled concurrently in Account Factory, through an asynchronous process, with up to five (5) account-related operations in progress simultaneously. Unmanaging accounts must be performed one account at a time.

note: d072. Concurrent account operations since 2022-12-16 (history row).

claim: A limit of 10 SCPs per OU applies to the OUs in an AWS Control Tower landing zone.
question: How many SCPs can be attached to an OU in an AWS Control Tower landing zone?

qualifiers.scope: per OU in the landing zone

evidence.quote: A limit of ten (10) SCPs per OU applies to OUs in your AWS Control Tower landing zone.

note: d072. Matches the Organizations SCP attachment limit of 10 after 2026-05-15 (organizations-scp-max-attached-per-entity).

claim: AWS Control Tower supports up to 10,000 accounts in the landing zone's organization, divided among all of its OUs.
question: How many accounts can an AWS Control Tower landing zone's organization hold?

qualifiers.scope: per landing zone organization, across all OUs

evidence.quote: AWS Control Tower supports up to 10,000 accounts in your landing zone's organization, divided among all of your OUs.

note: d072. The Organizations quota page lists AWS Control Tower | 10000 | No as a service with a separate account limit.

claim: An existing OU with more than 1000 directly nested accounts cannot be registered or re-registered in AWS Control Tower.
question: How many directly nested accounts can an OU have and still be registered in AWS Control Tower?

qualifiers.condition: registering or re-registering an existing OU

evidence.quote: Existing OUs with over 1000 directly nested accounts cannot be registered or re-registered in AWS Control Tower.

note: d072, d131. History 2024-08-30: up to 1000 accounts per OU.

claim: For the EnableControl and DisableControl APIs the limit is 100 concurrent operations, of which 10 can be in progress simultaneously while the rest are queued.
question: How many EnableControl or DisableControl operations can be in progress at the same time?

qualifiers.scope: per landing zone, control API calls

evidence.quote: When calling a control API to activate or deactivate a control, the limit for `EnableControl` and `DisableControl` updates in AWS Control Tower is one hundred (100) concurrent operations. Ten operations (10) can be in progress simultaneously, with the remaining operations queued.

claim: There is no additional charge for using AWS Control Tower; you pay only for the AWS services it enables and the services you use in the landing zone, for example Service Catalog for Account Factory and CloudTrail for events.
question: What does AWS Control Tower itself cost, and what do you pay for?

evidence.quote: No additional charge exists for using AWS Control Tower. You only pay for the AWS services enabled by AWS Control Tower, and the services you use in your landing zone. For example, you pay for Service Catalog for provisioning accounts with Account Factory, and AWS CloudTrail for events tracked in your landing zone.

claim: When you set up AWS Control Tower, AWS Organizations and IAM Identity Center come at no additional charge, but you pay by usage for services such as Service Catalog, CloudTrail, AWS Config, CloudWatch, SNS, S3 and Amazon VPC.
question: Which underlying services create charges when you use AWS Control Tower?

values.display: AWS Service Catalog, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config

qualifiers.condition: based on your usage of these services

evidence.quote: While some AWS services, such as AWS Organizations and AWS IAM Identity Center, come at no additional charge, you will pay for services, such as AWS Service Catalog, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS), Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), and Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC), based on your usage of these services.

claim: Running ephemeral workloads from accounts in AWS Control Tower can increase AWS Config costs, because AWS Config records the configuration changes of creating and deleting these temporary resources.
question: Why can ephemeral workloads raise costs in AWS Control Tower accounts?

values.display: increase in costs from AWS Config
values.spoken: an increase in AWS Config costs

qualifiers.condition: ephemeral workloads such as Spot Instances, EMR jobs and Auto Scaling

evidence.quote: If you are running ephemeral workloads from accounts in AWS Control Tower, you may see an increase in costs from AWS Config as it records configuration changes associated with creating and deleting these temporary resources.

claim: When you set up a landing zone, AWS Control Tower creates an organization-level CloudTrail trail that logs all events for the management account and all member accounts. Before landing zone version 3.0 (2022-07-29) it created a member account trail in each account.
question: What kind of CloudTrail trail does AWS Control Tower create for the landing zone, and what did older versions do?

values.display: a member account trail in each account
values.spoken: a member account trail in each account

evidence.quote: AWS Control Tower sets up a new CloudTrail trail when you set up a landing zone. It is an *organization-level trail*, which means that it logs all events for the management account and all member accounts in the organization.

In AWS Control Tower releases before landing zone version 3.0, AWS Control Tower created a member account trail in each account. When you update to release 3.0, your CloudTrail trail becomes an organization trail.

changed.was: a member account trail in each account

note: d133. Date from the version 3.0 history row (July 29, 2022).

claim: With the optional auto-enrollment feature, available for landing zone version 3.1 and above, an account moved into Control Tower automatically receives the baseline resources and control configurations of the destination OU; this applies to existing and newly created accounts.
question: What happens to an account moved into a registered OU when AWS Control Tower auto-enrollment is turned on?

qualifiers.scope: per account moved into a registered OU
qualifiers.condition: auto-enrollment turned on; landing zone version 3.1 and above

evidence.quote: The account automatically receives baseline resources and control configurations from the destination organizational unit (OU) in AWS Control Tower.
The account auto-enrollment feature is available for landing zones of version 3.1 and above.
This applies to both existing accounts and newly created accounts (which are created in the organization root by default).
